intent: Wipe the assumption off the screen: the table that puts the Horn of Africa above Arabia, the word ARABIA erased, then the wild herd on the wrong continent and the milk in every Somali town.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which nation is home to the MOST camels?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which nation is home to the most camels?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Somalia. More than 7 million camels, the most of any nation, in a country of 18 million people.

lines.direction: pull back over the Horn and Arabia; the ARABIA? plate waits at the bottom; bars build on 'Sudan' with Somalia on top; on 'Saudi' the ARABIA? plate wipes away and the Saudi flag-ball slumps; Somalia pulses
lines.text: Sudan follows with about 5 million, Kenya around 3. Saudi Arabia, the land of the camel, keeps under 2 million.

lines.direction: drift south-east towards the Indian Ocean; the Australian flag-ball thinks on 'Australia'; the 300,000 FERAL card on 'feral'; a cactus-desert sticker on 'outback'
lines.text: And Australia? Camels are not native there, yet about 300,000 feral ones roam the outback, more than anywhere.

lines.direction: push back onto Somalia; a meat-on-bone sticker on 'food' becomes a money bag on 'wealth' and a milk glass on 'milk' with the tag; the Somali flag-ball grins; Somalia pulses
lines.text: In Somalia the camel is food, transport and wealth; its milk is sold in every town.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
